setup: CREATE TABLE items AS SELECT i::DECIMAL(18,0) AS item_id, ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'][1 + i] AS kind FROM range(4) t(i)
CREATE TABLE buys AS SELECT i::BIGINT AS buy_id, (i % 8)::BIGINT AS user_id, ((i * 3) % 4)::DECIMAL(18,0) AS item_id, TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' + to_days((i * 5)::INTEGER) AS ts FROM range(120) t(i)
input.pql: PREDICT LIST_DISTINCT(buys.item_id, 0, 30, days) RANK TOP 2 FOR EACH users.user_id

expect.today: recorded at the reference 6298913c on DuckDB, SQLite and Postgres: asked as one binary classification per candidate (COUNT(buys.* WHERE buys.item_id = <c>, 0, 30, days) > 0 on the DECIMAL(18,0) key), one call each, three calls; the scripted endpoint answers each with probabilities (input.probabilities), and each user ranks the two candidates likeliest first (RANK TOP 2) (contract/t210-target-vectors.json holds the labels)

why: A ranking over a DECIMAL(18,0) key column (items.item_id, which buys.item_id references), candidates=[0, 1, 2]: each candidate's question filters buys by its key, a comparison of a decimal column, which the core's rule target_filter refuses where the reference answers (T2.8's review, P3-1)
